decisions.reason: As a sensor module in the firm’s core modular electronics domain, it fits existing knowledge well and the standalone product page suggests enough initial commitment to keep learning and improve it rather than withdraw quickly.
Because it directly replaces an earlier voltage measurement module, it builds on very strong prior knowledge and an existing customer need, making near-term withdrawal unlikely.

The MQTT proxy is adjacent to the firm’s hardware ecosystem and likely valuable for integration, but as a somewhat more software-centric offering it carries a bit more uncertainty even though absorptive capacity is still high.
A CAN bus interface module matches the firm’s established competence in industrial communication modules, so the firm is likely to retain it and refine it as market feedback comes in.
A carbon dioxide sensor module is closely related to the firm’s sensor know-how and complements other environmental sensing products, which supports continued commercialization.

The touch panel accessory is somewhat more peripheral than core sensing and interface modules, but it still leverages the firm’s electronics knowledge and is likely to be kept while demand is tested further.
